context:
Goal: a finding leaves the child repo once it is filed here, so nothing is filed twice or lost.
Problem (rule): the plan has the child's own triage remove each filed line, but an earlier route has a claude-settings session push into each child under your override, and only you can pick.
Based on (read): every filed line cites its source repo and file; the child's triage removes a line when that cite is on claude-settings main or the record branch.
Based on (read): the shared template skills/project-ops/templates/operating-model.md, which each child copies, needs one line for route a.
Departs from: main — adds a clearing step for child findings filed here.

lastAnswer.note: either works -as claude settings u shudnt need an override for B, u can just add the repo to ur session environment snd thrn act

options.gain: No session writes into another repo, and no override is needed.
options.how: Each child's triage removes a line once its cite shows up in claude-settings; a lane adds that line to the shared template. Route b stays the fallback for a child with no triage running.
options.label: Each child's triage clears its own (Recommended)
options.lose: A child whose triage is not running keeps its filed lines until one runs.

options.gain: Every child clears at once, with or without a running triage.
options.how: A claude-settings session pushes the removals into each child's record branch, under one override you type per repo.
options.label: A one-time push into each child
options.lose: You type an override per repo, and a session writes outside its own repo.

ref: plan PR #2974, owner act b; item 490 route
reply: Closed 00:51 CST Nov 13 by triage: either works. For b, a claude-settings session adds the child repo to its own session and pushes there, with no override. Sent to lane outbox-aggregate-plan.
title: Who removes a child repo's finding once claude-settings has filed it?
why: Option b writes into other repos, which needs your override each time.
